To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed a multiframe model for the scheduling of real-time tasks, we have established that a significant improvement can be achieved in the schedulability bounds for the preemptive, fixed priority scheduling policy, we have developed efficient algorithms to solve the schedulability analysis problem, we have developed a prototype implementation of the multiframe model, and we are in the process of evaluating its performance on real-time applications.
a real-time task model that allows the execution time to vary from one invocation to the next can significantly improve the schedulability of a system.
the multiframe model for periodic tasks can improve the schedulability of the preemptive fixed-priority policy.

a multiframe model for a class of real-time tasks and the corresponding schedulability problem.

the following issues: (1) the schedulability of multiframe tasks, (2) the schedulablity of periodic tasks with variable execution times, and (3) the schedulabilty of periodic tasks with non-uniform periods.
a new real-time task model and its application to the schedulability analysis for real-time tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the multiframe model is more efficient than the periodic model in that it allows more tasks to be scheduled on a given set of processors, while at the same time it is more realistic in that it allows the worst-case execution of a task to be less pessimistic.
the multiframe model can be used to improve the schedulability of real-time tasks.
, if we are to consider a task with a multiframe execution time model, we should use a preemptive fixed priority policy and we should use our model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our model is more general than the Liu and Layland model and the schedulability bound is tighter than that for the Liu and Layand model.
the multiframe real-time model is more practical than the periodic model and the schedulability analysis for this model is more efficient than that of the periodic task model.
our utilization bound is the best known bound for the preemptive priority scheduling policy for real-time systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the worst-case utilization bound can be improved by considering the average behavior of a task in the scheduling policy.
by considering the execution times of a real-time task as varying over time, we can significantly improve the utilization bound for the preemptive scheduling policy.

the worst-case execution-time model is not always the most appropriate model for real-time systems and a multiframe model can provide a more accurate model of real-time systems and lead to a more efficient scheduling policy.
